questions.q:
Two different aqueous solutions of $\text{HCl}$, A and B, are available. In separate experiments, $25\text{ mL}$ of a $0.4\text{ M}$ $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ solution requires exactly $10\text{ mL}$ of solution A for complete neutralization, and $40\text{ mL}$ of solution B for complete neutralization.
The volume of solution A (in $\text{mL}$) that must be mixed with solution B to prepare $1000\text{ mL}$ of a $0.8\text{ M}$ $\text{HCl}$ solution is ____.
(Assume volumes are additive)
questions.question:
Two different aqueous solutions of $\text{HCl}$, A and B, are available. In separate experiments, $25\text{ mL}$ of a $0.4\text{ M}$ $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ solution requires exactly $10\text{ mL}$ of solution A for complete neutralization, and $40\text{ mL}$ of solution B for complete neutralization.
The volume of solution A (in $\text{mL}$) that must be mixed with solution B to prepare $1000\text{ mL}$ of a $0.8\text{ M}$ $\text{HCl}$ solution is ____.
(Assume volumes are additive)
questions.solution:
The neutralization reaction is $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 + 2\text{HCl} \rightarrow 2\text{NaCl} + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2$.

Millimoles of $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 = 25 \times 0.4 = 10 \text{ mmol}$.

Millimoles of $\text{HCl}$ required for complete neutralization $= 2 \times 10 = 20 \text{ mmol}$.

For solution A:

$M_A \times 10 = 20 \Rightarrow M_A = 2 \text{ M}$

For solution B:

$M_B \times 40 = 20 \Rightarrow M_B = 0.5 \text{ M}$

Let $V_A$ be the volume of solution A to be mixed. The volume of solution B will be $(1000 - V_A) \text{ mL}$.

Total millimoles of $\text{HCl}$ in the final solution $= 1000 \times 0.8 = 800 \text{ mmol}$.

Using the mixing formula $M_A V_A + M_B V_B = M_{mix} V_{mix}$:

$2 V_A + 0.5 (1000 - V_A) = 800$

$2 V_A + 500 - 0.5 V_A = 800$

$1.5 V_A = 300$

$V_A = 200 \text{ mL}$

Answer: $200$

A $0.54$ g sample of an alloy containing $90\%$ silver by mass was dissolved in concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$. All the silver in the solution was then completely precipitated as $\text{AgSCN}$ by the addition of $25$ mL of a $\text{KSCN}$ solution. The molarity of the $\text{KSCN}$ solution is $x \times 10^{-2} \text{ mol L}^{-1}$. The value of $x$ is ____.
(Given: Atomic mass of $\text{Ag} = 108 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.question:
A $0.54$ g sample of an alloy containing $90\%$ silver by mass was dissolved in concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$. All the silver in the solution was then completely precipitated as $\text{AgSCN}$ by the addition of $25$ mL of a $\text{KSCN}$ solution. The molarity of the $\text{KSCN}$ solution is $x \times 10^{-2} \text{ mol L}^{-1}$. The value of $x$ is ____.
(Given: Atomic mass of $\text{Ag} = 108 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
Mass of the alloy sample = $0.54 \text{ g}$

Mass of silver in the alloy = $90\%$ of $0.54 \text{ g} = \dfrac{90}{100} \times 0.54 = 0.486 \text{ g}$

Moles of silver = $\dfrac{0.486}{108} = 0.0045 \text{ mol}$

The reaction for the precipitation of silver as $\text{AgSCN}$ is:

$\text{Ag}^{+} + \text{SCN}^{-} \rightarrow \text{AgSCN}$

From the stoichiometry of the reaction, moles of $\text{KSCN}$ required = moles of $\text{Ag}^{+} = 0.0045 \text{ mol}$

Volume of $\text{KSCN}$ solution = $25 \text{ mL} = 0.025 \text{ L}$

Molarity of $\text{KSCN}$ solution = $\dfrac{\text{Moles of KSCN}}{\text{Volume in L}} = \dfrac{0.0045}{0.025} = 0.18 \text{ mol L}^{-1}$

Comparing this with $x \times 10^{-2} \text{ mol L}^{-1}$, we get:

$0.18 = x \times 10^{-2} \Rightarrow x = 18$

Answer: $18$
questions.explanation:
Mass of the alloy sample = $0.54 \text{ g}$

The reaction for the precipitation of silver as $\text{AgSCN}$ is:

$\text{Ag}^{+} + \text{SCN}^{-} \rightarrow \text{AgSCN}$

From the stoichiometry of the reaction, moles of $\text{KSCN}$ required = moles of $\text{Ag}^{+} = 0.0045 \text{ mol}$

Molarity of $\text{KSCN}$ solution = $\dfrac{\text{Moles of KSCN}}{\text{Volume in L}} = \dfrac{0.0045}{0.025} = 0.18 \text{ mol L}^{-1}$

Comparing this with $x \times 10^{-2} \text{ mol L}^{-1}$, we get:

$0.18 = x \times 10^{-2} \Rightarrow x = 18$

Answer: $18$

questions.q: A volume of $15.0\text{ mL}$ of $0.04\text{ M}$ aqueous selenium dioxide ($\text{SeO}_2$) reacts exactly with $30.0\text{ mL}$ of $0.08\text{ M}$ $\text{CrSO}_4$ solution. In the reaction, $\text{Cr}^{2+}$ is oxidised to $\text{Cr}^{3+}$. The final oxidation state of selenium in the product is ____.
questions.question: A volume of $15.0\text{ mL}$ of $0.04\text{ M}$ aqueous selenium dioxide ($\text{SeO}_2$) reacts exactly with $30.0\text{ mL}$ of $0.08\text{ M}$ $\text{CrSO}_4$ solution. In the reaction, $\text{Cr}^{2+}$ is oxidised to $\text{Cr}^{3+}$. The final oxidation state of selenium in the product is ____.
questions.solution:
Millimoles of $\text{SeO}_2 = 15.0 \times 0.04 = 0.6$

Millimoles of $\text{CrSO}_4 = 30.0 \times 0.08 = 2.4$

The oxidation state of $\text{Se}$ in $\text{SeO}_2$ is $+4$. Let the final oxidation state of $\text{Se}$ be $x$.

The $n$-factor for $\text{SeO}_2$ is $4 - x$.

The oxidation state of $\text{Cr}$ changes from $+2$ to $+3$, so the $n$-factor for $\text{CrSO}_4$ is $3 - 2 = 1$.

Equating the milliequivalents of the oxidizing and reducing agents:

$0.6 \times (4 - x) = 2.4 \times 1$

$4 - x = \dfrac{2.4}{0.6}$

$4 - x = 4$

$x = 0$

The final oxidation state of selenium is $0$.

Answer: $0$

questions.q:
The chromate ion ($\text{CrO}_4^{2-}$) present in the wastewater of a chrome plating plant is reduced to insoluble chromium hydroxide, $\text{Cr(OH)}_3$, by the addition of sodium dithionite ($\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_4$) in a basic medium. The unbalanced ionic equation is:
$\text{S}_2\text{O}_4^{2-} + \text{CrO}_4^{2-} + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{SO}_3^{2-} + \text{Cr(OH)}_3$
If $50\text{ L}$ of wastewater requires $522\text{ g}$ of $\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_4$ for complete precipitation of chromium, the molarity of $\text{CrO}_4^{2-}$ in the wastewater is $x \times 10^{-2}\text{ M}$. The value of $x$ is ____.
(Given: Molar mass of $\text{Na} = 23\text{ g mol}^{-1}$, $\text{S} = 32\text{ g mol}^{-1}$, $\text{O} = 16\text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.question:
The chromate ion ($\text{CrO}_4^{2-}$) present in the wastewater of a chrome plating plant is reduced to insoluble chromium hydroxide, $\text{Cr(OH)}_3$, by the addition of sodium dithionite ($\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_4$) in a basic medium. The unbalanced ionic equation is:
$\text{S}_2\text{O}_4^{2-} + \text{CrO}_4^{2-} + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{SO}_3^{2-} + \text{Cr(OH)}_3$
If $50\text{ L}$ of wastewater requires $522\text{ g}$ of $\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_4$ for complete precipitation of chromium, the molarity of $\text{CrO}_4^{2-}$ in the wastewater is $x \times 10^{-2}\text{ M}$. The value of $x$ is ____.
(Given: Molar mass of $\text{Na} = 23\text{ g mol}^{-1}$, $\text{S} = 32\text{ g mol}^{-1}$, $\text{O} = 16\text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
The oxidation state of $\text{S}$ in $\text{S}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$ is $+3$ and in $\text{SO}_3^{2-}$ is $+4$.
Change in oxidation state per $\text{S}$ atom $= 1$.
The n-factor of $\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_4 = 1 \times 2 = 2$.

The oxidation state of $\text{Cr}$ in $\text{CrO}_4^{2-}$ is $+6$ and in $\text{Cr(OH)}_3$ is $+3$.
Change in oxidation state per $\text{Cr}$ atom $= 3$.
The n-factor of $\text{CrO}_4^{2-} = 3$.

Molar mass of $\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_4 = 2 \times 23 + 2 \times 32 + 4 \times 16 = 174 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$.
Moles of $\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_4 = \dfrac{522}{174} = 3 \text{ mol}$.

Using the law of equivalence:
Equivalents of $\text{CrO}_4^{2-} =$ Equivalents of $\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_4$
Moles of $\text{CrO}_4^{2-} \times 3 = 3 \times 2$
Moles of $\text{CrO}_4^{2-} = 2 \text{ mol}$.

Molarity of $\text{CrO}_4^{2-}$ in the wastewater is:
$M = \dfrac{\text{Moles}}{\text{Volume in L}} = \dfrac{2}{50} = 0.04 \text{ M} = 4 \times 10^{-2} \text{ M}$.

Comparing with $x \times 10^{-2} \text{ M}$, we get $x = 4$.

Answer: $4$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Calcium oxalate is insoluble in water. This property is used to determine the amount of calcium ions in blood. The calcium oxalate precipitated and isolated from a $10\text{ mL}$ sample of blood is dissolved in dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ and titrated against a standard $\text{KMnO}_4$ solution. If the titration requires $24\text{ mL}$ of $0.001\text{ M}$ $\text{KMnO}_4$ solution, the mass of calcium in $\text{mg}$ present per $100\text{ mL}$ of blood is ____.
(Given: Molar mass of $\text{Ca} = 40\text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.question:
Calcium oxalate is insoluble in water. This property is used to determine the amount of calcium ions in blood. The calcium oxalate precipitated and isolated from a $10\text{ mL}$ sample of blood is dissolved in dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ and titrated against a standard $\text{KMnO}_4$ solution. If the titration requires $24\text{ mL}$ of $0.001\text{ M}$ $\text{KMnO}_4$ solution, the mass of calcium in $\text{mg}$ present per $100\text{ mL}$ of blood is ____.
(Given: Molar mass of $\text{Ca} = 40\text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
The redox reaction between permanganate and oxalate in acidic medium is given by:

$2\text{MnO}_4^- + 5\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-} + 16\text{H}^+ \rightarrow 2\text{Mn}^{2+} + 10\text{CO}_2 + 8\text{H}_2\text{O}$

The n-factor for $\text{KMnO}_4$ is $5$ (as $\text{Mn}$ goes from $+7$ to $+2$) and for $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$ is $2$ (as $\text{C}$ goes from $+3$ to $+4$ for two carbon atoms).

Milliequivalents of $\text{KMnO}_4$ used in the titration:

$\text{meq}(\text{KMnO}_4) = \text{Molarity} \times \text{n-factor} \times \text{Volume in mL}$

$\text{meq}(\text{KMnO}_4) = 0.001 \times 5 \times 24 = 0.12 \text{ meq}$

By the law of equivalence, milliequivalents of $\text{CaC}_2\text{O}_4$ = milliequivalents of $\text{KMnO}_4$ = $0.12 \text{ meq}$.

Millimoles of $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ in $10 \text{ mL}$ of blood = Millimoles of $\text{CaC}_2\text{O}_4$ = $\dfrac{0.12}{2} = 0.06 \text{ mmol}$.

Millimoles of $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ in $100 \text{ mL}$ of blood = $0.06 \times \dfrac{100}{10} = 0.6 \text{ mmol}$.

Mass of calcium in $100 \text{ mL}$ of blood = Millimoles $\times$ Molar mass

Mass = $0.6 \text{ mmol} \times 40 \text{ mg mmol}^{-1} = 24 \text{ mg}$.

Answer: $24$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
What mass of $\text{KMnO}_4$ (in mg) is required to completely react with $50\text{ mL}$ of $0.1\text{ M}$ aqueous oxalic acid ($\text{H}_2\text{C}_2\text{O}_4$) solution in the presence of dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$?
(Given: Molar mass of $\text{KMnO}_4 = 158\text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.question:
What mass of $\text{KMnO}_4$ (in mg) is required to completely react with $50\text{ mL}$ of $0.1\text{ M}$ aqueous oxalic acid ($\text{H}_2\text{C}_2\text{O}_4$) solution in the presence of dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$?
(Given: Molar mass of $\text{KMnO}_4 = 158\text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
The balanced half-reactions in acidic medium are:

$\text{MnO}_4^- + 8\text{H}^+ + 5\text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{Mn}^{2+} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$

$\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-} \rightarrow 2\text{CO}_2 + 2\text{e}^-$

The n-factor for $\text{KMnO}_4$ is $5$ and for $\text{H}_2\text{C}_2\text{O}_4$ is $2$.

Equating the milli-equivalents of both reactants:

$\text{meq of KMnO}_4 = \text{meq of H}_2\text{C}_2\text{O}_4$

$n \times 5 = M \times V \times 2$

$n \times 5 = 0.1 \times 50 \times 2$

$5n = 10$

$n = 2 \text{ mmol}$

The mass of $\text{KMnO}_4$ required is:

$\text{Mass} = n \times \text{Molar mass}$

$\text{Mass} = 2 \times 10^{-3} \text{ mol} \times 158 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$

$\text{Mass} = 316 \times 10^{-3} \text{ g} = 316 \text{ mg}$

Answer: $316$

The volume of $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$ solution required to completely convert the $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ into $\text{Ca(H}_2\text{PO}_4)_2$ is ____ $\text{mL}$.
questions.question: An aqueous solution of $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ ($10\text{ mL}$ of $0.04\text{ M}$) is treated with a $0.02\text{ M}$ aqueous solution of $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$. The volume of $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$ solution required to completely convert the $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ into $\text{Ca(H}_2\text{PO}_4)_2$ is ____ $\text{mL}$.
questions.solution:
The balanced chemical equation for the reaction is:

$\text{Ca(OH)}_2 + 2\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 \rightarrow \text{Ca(H}_2\text{PO}_4)_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$

From the stoichiometry, $1\text{ mole}$ of $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$ reacts with $2\text{ moles}$ of $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$.

Millimoles of $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 = M \times V = 0.04 \times 10 = 0.4\text{ mmol}$.

Millimoles of $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$ required $= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 0.4 = 0.2\text{ mmol}$.

Volume of $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$ required $= \dfrac{\text{Millimoles}}{\text{Molarity}} = \dfrac{0.2}{0.02} = 10\text{ mL}$.

Alternatively, using the concept of equivalents:
In the conversion of $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ to $\text{Ca(H}_2\text{PO}_4)_2$, one $\text{H}^+$ ion is replaced per molecule of $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$.
Thus, the n-factor of $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ is $1$.
The n-factor of $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$ is $2$.

Equating the milliequivalents:
$N_1 V_1 = N_2 V_2$
$(M_1 \times n_1) V_1 = (M_2 \times n_2) V_2$
$(0.04 \times 1) \times 10 = (0.02 \times 2) \times V$
$0.4 = 0.04 \times V$
$V = 10\text{ mL}$.

Answer: $10$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The mass of oxalic acid crystals ($\text{H}_2\text{C}_2\text{O}_4 \cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$) required to react completely with $100\text{ mL}$ of $0.2\text{ M}$ $\text{KMnO}_4$ solution in acidic medium is $x \times 10^{-1}\text{ g}$.

Given: Molar mass of $\text{H}_2\text{C}_2\text{O}_4 \cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is $126\text{ g mol}^{-1}$.

The value of $x$ is ____.
questions.question:
The mass of oxalic acid crystals ($\text{H}_2\text{C}_2\text{O}_4 \cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$) required to react completely with $100\text{ mL}$ of $0.2\text{ M}$ $\text{KMnO}_4$ solution in acidic medium is $x \times 10^{-1}\text{ g}$.

Given: Molar mass of $\text{H}_2\text{C}_2\text{O}_4 \cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is $126\text{ g mol}^{-1}$.

The value of $x$ is ____.
questions.solution:
The n-factor of $\text{KMnO}_4$ in acidic medium is $5$.

The n-factor of oxalic acid ($\text{H}_2\text{C}_2\text{O}_4 \cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$) is $2$.

According to the law of equivalence:

Equivalents of $\text{KMnO}_4$ = Equivalents of $\text{H}_2\text{C}_2\text{O}_4 \cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$

$\text{Molarity} \times \text{Volume (in L)} \times \text{n-factor} = \dfrac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Equivalent mass}}$

$0.2 \times \dfrac{100}{1000} \times 5 = \dfrac{W}{126 / 2}$

$0.1 = \dfrac{W}{63}$

$W = 6.3\text{ g}$

Given that the mass is $x \times 10^{-1}\text{ g}$, we have:

$6.3 = x \times 10^{-1}$

$x = 63$

Answer: $63$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Borax ($\text{Na}_2\text{B}_4\text{O}_7 \cdot 10\text{H}_2\text{O}$) acts as a base in aqueous solution due to the following reaction:
$\text{B}_4\text{O}_7^{2-} + 7\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 4\text{H}_3\text{BO}_3 + 2\text{OH}^-$
The mass of borax required to completely neutralize $20 \text{ mL}$ of $0.1 \text{ M}$ aqueous hydrochloric acid solution is ____ $\text{mg}$.
(Given atomic masses in $\text{g mol}^{-1}$: $\text{H} = 1$, $\text{B} = 11$, $\text{O} = 16$, $\text{Na} = 23$)
questions.question:
Borax ($\text{Na}_2\text{B}_4\text{O}_7 \cdot 10\text{H}_2\text{O}$) acts as a base in aqueous solution due to the following reaction:
$\text{B}_4\text{O}_7^{2-} + 7\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 4\text{H}_3\text{BO}_3 + 2\text{OH}^-$
The mass of borax required to completely neutralize $20 \text{ mL}$ of $0.1 \text{ M}$ aqueous hydrochloric acid solution is ____ $\text{mg}$.
(Given atomic masses in $\text{g mol}^{-1}$: $\text{H} = 1$, $\text{B} = 11$, $\text{O} = 16$, $\text{Na} = 23$)
questions.solution:
The given reaction of borax in aqueous solution is:
$\text{B}_4\text{O}_7^{2-} + 7\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 4\text{H}_3\text{BO}_3 + 2\text{OH}^-$

This indicates that $1$ mole of borax produces $2$ moles of $\text{OH}^-$ ions, which will neutralize $2$ moles of $\text{H}^+$ from $\text{HCl}$.

The number of millimoles of $\text{HCl}$ is:
$n_{\text{HCl}} = M \times V = 0.1 \text{ M} \times 20 \text{ mL} = 2 \text{ mmol}$

Since $1$ mole of borax neutralizes $2$ moles of $\text{HCl}$, the millimoles of borax required is:
$n_{\text{borax}} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times n_{\text{HCl}} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2 = 1 \text{ mmol}$

The molar mass of borax ($\text{Na}_2\text{B}_4\text{O}_7 \cdot 10\text{H}_2\text{O}$) is:
$M = 2(23) + 4(11) + 7(16) + 10(18)$
$M = 46 + 44 + 112 + 180 = 382 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$

The mass of borax required is:
$\text{Mass} = n_{\text{borax}} \times M = 1 \text{ mmol} \times 382 \text{ g mol}^{-1} = 382 \text{ mg}$

Answer: $382$

questions.q: A $40\text{ mL}$ solution of a $0.05\text{ M}$ metal salt reacts completely with $30\text{ mL}$ of a $0.1\text{ M}$ sodium sulphite ($\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_3$) solution. In the reaction, the sulphite ion is oxidized to the sulphate ion. If the oxidation state of the metal in the original salt is $+5$, the new oxidation state of the metal is ____.
questions.question: A $40\text{ mL}$ solution of a $0.05\text{ M}$ metal salt reacts completely with $30\text{ mL}$ of a $0.1\text{ M}$ sodium sulphite ($\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_3$) solution. In the reaction, the sulphite ion is oxidized to the sulphate ion. If the oxidation state of the metal in the original salt is $+5$, the new oxidation state of the metal is ____.
questions.solution:
Millimoles of metal salt = $40 \times 0.05 = 2$

Millimoles of sodium sulphite = $30 \times 0.1 = 3$

In the reaction, sulphite ion ($\text{SO}_3^{2-}$) is oxidized to sulphate ion ($\text{SO}_4^{2-}$). The oxidation state of sulphur changes from $+4$ to $+6$.

The n-factor for sodium sulphite is $6 - 4 = 2$.

Let the new oxidation state of the metal be $x$. The n-factor for the metal salt is $5 - x$.

According to the law of equivalence, milliequivalents of metal salt = milliequivalents of sodium sulphite.

$2 \times (5 - x) = 3 \times 2$

$5 - x = 3$

$x = 2$

Answer: $2$

$5 - x = 3$

$x = 2$

Answer: $2$

questions.q:
A $1.7\text{ g}$ sample of a hydrogen peroxide solution containing $x\%$ of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ by mass requires $x\text{ mL}$ of a $\text{KMnO}_4$ solution for complete oxidation under acidic conditions. The molarity of the $\text{KMnO}_4$ solution is $y \times 10^{-2}\text{ M}$. The value of $y$ is ____.
(Given: Molar mass of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ is $34\text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.question:
A $1.7\text{ g}$ sample of a hydrogen peroxide solution containing $x\%$ of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ by mass requires $x\text{ mL}$ of a $\text{KMnO}_4$ solution for complete oxidation under acidic conditions. The molarity of the $\text{KMnO}_4$ solution is $y \times 10^{-2}\text{ M}$. The value of $y$ is ____.
(Given: Molar mass of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ is $34\text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
Mass of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ in the sample = $\dfrac{x}{100} \times 1.7 = 0.017x\text{ g}$

Moles of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ = $\dfrac{0.017x}{34} = 5 \times 10^{-4}x$

In the oxidation of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ by $\text{KMnO}_4$, the n-factor of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ is $2$ (since $\text{O}_2^{2-} \rightarrow \text{O}_2 + 2e^-$).

Equivalents of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ = $2 \times 5 \times 10^{-4}x = 10^{-3}x$

For $\text{KMnO}_4$ in acidic medium, the n-factor is $5$ (since $\text{Mn}^{7+} + 5e^- \rightarrow \text{Mn}^{2+}$).

Molarity of $\text{KMnO}_4$ = $y \times 10^{-2}\text{ M}$

Normality of $\text{KMnO}_4$ = $5 \times y \times 10^{-2}\text{ N}$

Volume of $\text{KMnO}_4$ = $x\text{ mL} = x \times 10^{-3}\text{ L}$

Equivalents of $\text{KMnO}_4$ = Normality $\times$ Volume = $5y \times 10^{-2} \times x \times 10^{-3} = 5xy \times 10^{-5}$

Equating the equivalents of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ and $\text{KMnO}_4$:

$10^{-3}x = 5xy \times 10^{-5}$

$10^{-3} = 5y \times 10^{-5}$

$100 = 5y$

$y = 20$

Answer: $20$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
A sample of $1.44 \text{ g}$ of ferrous oxalate ($\text{FeC}_2\text{O}_4$) is dissolved in dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$. The resulting solution requires $150 \text{ mL}$ of a $\text{KMnO}_4$ solution to reach the end point. The molarity of the $\text{KMnO}_4$ solution is $x \times 10^{-3} \text{ M}$. The value of $x$ is ____.
(Given: Molar mass of $\text{Fe} = 56 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$, $\text{C} = 12 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$, $\text{O} = 16 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.question:
A sample of $1.44 \text{ g}$ of ferrous oxalate ($\text{FeC}_2\text{O}_4$) is dissolved in dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$. The resulting solution requires $150 \text{ mL}$ of a $\text{KMnO}_4$ solution to reach the end point. The molarity of the $\text{KMnO}_4$ solution is $x \times 10^{-3} \text{ M}$. The value of $x$ is ____.
(Given: Molar mass of $\text{Fe} = 56 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$, $\text{C} = 12 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$, $\text{O} = 16 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
Molar mass of $\text{FeC}_2\text{O}_4 = 56 + 2 \times 12 + 4 \times 16 = 144 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$

Moles of $\text{FeC}_2\text{O}_4 = \dfrac{1.44}{144} = 0.01 \text{ mol}$

In acidic medium, $\text{FeC}_2\text{O}_4$ undergoes oxidation as follows:

$\text{Fe}^{2+} \rightarrow \text{Fe}^{3+} + e^{-}$

$\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-} \rightarrow 2\text{CO}_2 + 2e^{-}$

Total number of electrons lost per molecule of $\text{FeC}_2\text{O}_4$ is $3$. Thus, the n-factor of $\text{FeC}_2\text{O}_4$ is $3$.

Equivalents of $\text{FeC}_2\text{O}_4 = 0.01 \times 3 = 0.03 \text{ eq}$

In acidic medium, $\text{KMnO}_4$ acts as an oxidizing agent with an n-factor of $5$ ($\text{Mn}^{7+} + 5e^{-} \rightarrow \text{Mn}^{2+}$).

Equivalents of $\text{KMnO}_4 = \text{Molarity} \times \text{Volume (in L)} \times \text{n-factor}$

Equivalents of $\text{KMnO}_4 = M \times \dfrac{150}{1000} \times 5 = 0.75 M$

Equating the equivalents of both reactants:

$0.75 M = 0.03$

$M = \dfrac{0.03}{0.75} = 0.04 \text{ M}$

The molarity is given as $x \times 10^{-3} \text{ M}$.

$0.04 = x \times 10^{-3} \Rightarrow x = 40$

Answer: $40$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Magnesium hydroxide is formed as a white precipitate when aqueous solutions of sodium hydroxide and magnesium chloride are mixed. If $25\text{ mL}$ of $0.24\text{ M}$ $\text{NaOH}$ is mixed with $15\text{ mL}$ of $0.30\text{ M}$ $\text{MgCl}_2$, the mass of $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ formed is ____ mg. (Nearest integer)
(Given molar masses in $\text{g mol}^{-1}$: $\text{Mg} = 24, \text{O} = 16, \text{H} = 1$)
questions.question:
Magnesium hydroxide is formed as a white precipitate when aqueous solutions of sodium hydroxide and magnesium chloride are mixed. If $25\text{ mL}$ of $0.24\text{ M}$ $\text{NaOH}$ is mixed with $15\text{ mL}$ of $0.30\text{ M}$ $\text{MgCl}_2$, the mass of $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ formed is ____ mg. (Nearest integer)
(Given molar masses in $\text{g mol}^{-1}$: $\text{Mg} = 24, \text{O} = 16, \text{H} = 1$)
questions.solution:
The balanced chemical equation for the reaction is:

$\text{MgCl}_2 + 2\text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{Mg(OH)}_2 + 2\text{NaCl}$

Calculating the millimoles of the reactants:
Millimoles of $\text{NaOH} = 25\text{ mL} \times 0.24\text{ M} = 6.0\text{ mmol}$
Millimoles of $\text{MgCl}_2 = 15\text{ mL} \times 0.30\text{ M} = 4.5\text{ mmol}$

From the stoichiometry of the reaction, $1\text{ mmol}$ of $\text{MgCl}_2$ requires $2\text{ mmol}$ of $\text{NaOH}$.
For $4.5\text{ mmol}$ of $\text{MgCl}_2$, the required $\text{NaOH}$ is $9.0\text{ mmol}$. Since only $6.0\text{ mmol}$ of $\text{NaOH}$ is available, $\text{NaOH}$ is the limiting reagent.

The amount of $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ formed is determined by the limiting reagent:
Millimoles of $\text{Mg(OH)}_2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{millimoles of NaOH} = \dfrac{6.0}{2} = 3.0\text{ mmol}$

Molar mass of $\text{Mg(OH)}_2 = 24 + 2 \times (16 + 1) = 58\text{ g mol}^{-1}$

Mass of $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ formed $= 3.0\text{ mmol} \times 58\text{ g mol}^{-1} = 174\text{ mg}$

Answer: $174$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The molar mass of an unknown acid is $90 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$. In a titration experiment, $50 \text{ mL}$ of an aqueous solution of this acid containing $45 \text{ g}$ of the acid per litre was completely neutralized by $100 \text{ mL}$ of an aqueous solution of $\text{NaOH}$ containing $20 \text{ g}$ of $\text{NaOH}$ per litre.
Given: Molar mass of $\text{NaOH}$ is $40 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$.
The basicity of the acid is ____.
questions.question:
The molar mass of an unknown acid is $90 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$. In a titration experiment, $50 \text{ mL}$ of an aqueous solution of this acid containing $45 \text{ g}$ of the acid per litre was completely neutralized by $100 \text{ mL}$ of an aqueous solution of $\text{NaOH}$ containing $20 \text{ g}$ of $\text{NaOH}$ per litre.
Given: Molar mass of $\text{NaOH}$ is $40 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$.
The basicity of the acid is ____.
questions.solution:
Molarity of the acid solution = $\dfrac{45}{90} = 0.5 \text{ M}$

Molarity of the $\text{NaOH}$ solution = $\dfrac{20}{40} = 0.5 \text{ M}$

Let the basicity of the acid be $n$.

For complete neutralization, the number of equivalents of acid must equal the number of equivalents of base.

$n \times M_1 \times V_1 = 1 \times M_2 \times V_2$

$n \times 0.5 \times 50 = 1 \times 0.5 \times 100$

$25n = 50$

$n = 2$

Answer: $2$

$n \times M_1 \times V_1 = 1 \times M_2 \times V_2$

$n \times 0.5 \times 50 = 1 \times 0.5 \times 100$

$25n = 50$

$n = 2$

Answer: $2$

questions.question:

questions.solution:

Moles of $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ in $25\text{ mL}$ solution = $0.1 \times \dfrac{25}{250} = 0.01\text{ mol}$

Moles of $\text{NaOH}$ required = $2 \times$ moles of $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 = 2 \times 0.01 = 0.02\text{ mol}$

Volume of $0.5\text{ M NaOH}$ required = $\dfrac{\text{Moles}}{\text{Molarity}} = \dfrac{0.02}{0.5} = 0.04\text{ L} = 40\text{ mL}$

Answer: $40\text{ mL}$

questions.q: A $25\text{ mL}$ sample of $0.03\text{ M}$ $\text{HSO}_3^-$ solution requires $15\text{ mL}$ of a $0.02\text{ M}$ $\text{KMnO}_4$ solution for complete oxidation to $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ in a strongly acidic medium. When the same volume of the $\text{HSO}_3^-$ sample is titrated in a neutral medium, it requires $25\text{ mL}$ of the same $0.02\text{ M}$ $\text{KMnO}_4$ solution for complete oxidation. If the oxidation state of $\text{Mn}$ in the product formed in the acidic medium is $x$, and in the neutral medium is $y$, then the value of $(x+y)$ is ____.
questions.question: A $25\text{ mL}$ sample of $0.03\text{ M}$ $\text{HSO}_3^-$ solution requires $15\text{ mL}$ of a $0.02\text{ M}$ $\text{KMnO}_4$ solution for complete oxidation to $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ in a strongly acidic medium. When the same volume of the $\text{HSO}_3^-$ sample is titrated in a neutral medium, it requires $25\text{ mL}$ of the same $0.02\text{ M}$ $\text{KMnO}_4$ solution for complete oxidation. If the oxidation state of $\text{Mn}$ in the product formed in the acidic medium is $x$, and in the neutral medium is $y$, then the value of $(x+y)$ is ____.
questions.solution:
The oxidation of $\text{HSO}_3^-$ to $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ involves a change in the oxidation state of sulphur from $+4$ to $+6$.

The n-factor for $\text{HSO}_3^-$ is $2$.

Number of milliequivalents of $\text{HSO}_3^-$ is $25 \times 0.03 \times 2 = 1.5$.

In the strongly acidic medium, let the n-factor of $\text{KMnO}_4$ be $n_1$. Equating the milliequivalents:

$15 \times 0.02 \times n_1 = 1.5$

$0.3 n_1 = 1.5 \Rightarrow n_1 = 5$

The oxidation state of $\text{Mn}$ in $\text{KMnO}_4$ is $+7$. A change of $5$ means the oxidation state of $\text{Mn}$ in the product is $7 - 5 = 2$. Thus, $x = 2$.

In the neutral medium, let the n-factor of $\text{KMnO}_4$ be $n_2$. Equating the milliequivalents:

$25 \times 0.02 \times n_2 = 1.5$

$0.5 n_2 = 1.5 \Rightarrow n_2 = 3$

A change of $3$ means the oxidation state of $\text{Mn}$ in the product is $7 - 3 = 4$. Thus, $y = 4$.

The value of $(x+y)$ is $2 + 4 = 6$.

Answer: $6$

$n = 3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
A $1.43 \text{ g}$ sample of hydrated sodium carbonate, $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \cdot x\text{H}_2\text{O}$, is dissolved in water to prepare $100 \text{ mL}$ of solution. A $20 \text{ mL}$ portion of this solution requires $20 \text{ mL}$ of $0.1 \text{ M}$ $\text{HCl}$ solution for complete neutralization. The value of $x$ is ____.
(Given atomic masses in $\text{g mol}^{-1}$: $\text{Na} = 23, \text{C} = 12, \text{O} = 16, \text{H} = 1$)
questions.question:
A $1.43 \text{ g}$ sample of hydrated sodium carbonate, $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \cdot x\text{H}_2\text{O}$, is dissolved in water to prepare $100 \text{ mL}$ of solution. A $20 \text{ mL}$ portion of this solution requires $20 \text{ mL}$ of $0.1 \text{ M}$ $\text{HCl}$ solution for complete neutralization. The value of $x$ is ____.
(Given atomic masses in $\text{g mol}^{-1}$: $\text{Na} = 23, \text{C} = 12, \text{O} = 16, \text{H} = 1$)
questions.solution:
The balanced chemical equation for the neutralization is:

$\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 + 2\text{HCl} \rightarrow 2\text{NaCl} + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2$

Millimoles of $\text{HCl}$ used $= 20 \text{ mL} \times 0.1 \text{ M} = 2 \text{ mmol}$

From the stoichiometry of the reaction, $1 \text{ mole}$ of $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ reacts with $2 \text{ moles}$ of $\text{HCl}$.

Millimoles of $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ in $20 \text{ mL}$ solution $= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2 \text{ mmol} = 1 \text{ mmol}$

Millimoles of $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ in $100 \text{ mL}$ solution $= 1 \text{ mmol} \times \dfrac{100}{20} = 5 \text{ mmol} = 5 \times 10^{-3} \text{ mol}$

The molar mass of the hydrated salt $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \cdot x\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is:

$M = \dfrac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Moles}} = \dfrac{1.43 \text{ g}}{5 \times 10^{-3} \text{ mol}} = 286 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$

The molar mass of anhydrous $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 = 2(23) + 12 + 3(16) = 106 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$

Equating the molar mass of the hydrate:

$106 + 18x = 286$

$18x = 180$

$x = 10$

Answer: $10$

questions.q:
The density of a concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ solution is $1.60 \text{ g mL}^{-1}$. A $5.0 \text{ mL}$ sample of this acid is diluted to $1.0 \text{ L}$ with distilled water. It is found that $25 \text{ mL}$ of this diluted acid requires $20 \text{ mL}$ of $0.1 \text{ M NaOH}$ solution for complete neutralization. The mass percentage of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ in the original acid solution is _____. (Nearest integer)
(Given: Molar mass of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 = 98 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.question:
The density of a concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ solution is $1.60 \text{ g mL}^{-1}$. A $5.0 \text{ mL}$ sample of this acid is diluted to $1.0 \text{ L}$ with distilled water. It is found that $25 \text{ mL}$ of this diluted acid requires $20 \text{ mL}$ of $0.1 \text{ M NaOH}$ solution for complete neutralization. The mass percentage of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ in the original acid solution is _____. (Nearest integer)
(Given: Molar mass of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 = 98 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
For the neutralization reaction between $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ and $\text{NaOH}$:

Equivalents of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ = Equivalents of $\text{NaOH}$

Let the molarity of the diluted $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ solution be $M$. Since the $n$-factor of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is $2$ and that of $\text{NaOH}$ is $1$:

$2 \times M \times 25 = 1 \times 0.1 \times 20$

$50M = 2 \Rightarrow M = 0.04 \text{ mol L}^{-1}$

The total volume of the diluted acid is $1.0 \text{ L}$, so the total moles of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ in the solution is:

$\text{Moles of } \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 = 0.04 \text{ mol L}^{-1} \times 1.0 \text{ L} = 0.04 \text{ mol}$

Mass of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ present in the $5.0 \text{ mL}$ concentrated sample:

$\text{Mass} = 0.04 \text{ mol} \times 98 \text{ g mol}^{-1} = 3.92 \text{ g}$

The mass of the $5.0 \text{ mL}$ concentrated acid solution is:

$\text{Mass of solution} = \text{Volume} \times \text{Density} = 5.0 \text{ mL} \times 1.60 \text{ g mL}^{-1} = 8.0 \text{ g}$

The mass percentage of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ in the original acid solution is:

$\text{Mass \%} = \dfrac{3.92}{8.0} \times 100 = 49\%$

Answer: $49$

questions.q: A volume of $20 \text{ mL}$ of $0.1 \text{ M}$ $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ solution completely neutralizes $10 \text{ mL}$ of a dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ solution. The volume of water that must be added to $300 \text{ mL}$ of this $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ solution in order to make its concentration exactly $0.05 \text{ M}$ is ____ $\text{mL}$. (Assume volumes are additive)
questions.question: A volume of $20 \text{ mL}$ of $0.1 \text{ M}$ $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ solution completely neutralizes $10 \text{ mL}$ of a dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ solution. The volume of water that must be added to $300 \text{ mL}$ of this $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ solution in order to make its concentration exactly $0.05 \text{ M}$ is ____ $\text{mL}$. (Assume volumes are additive)
questions.solution:
The balanced chemical equation for the complete neutralization is:

$\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2$

From the stoichiometry, $1$ mole of $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ reacts with $1$ mole of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$.

Number of millimoles of $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 = M \times V = 0.1 \text{ M} \times 20 \text{ mL} = 2 \text{ mmol}$.

Therefore, the number of millimoles of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ in $10 \text{ mL}$ of the solution is also $2 \text{ mmol}$.

Molarity of the initial $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ solution ($M_1$) = $\dfrac{2 \text{ mmol}}{10 \text{ mL}} = 0.2 \text{ M}$.

For the dilution of $300 \text{ mL}$ of this $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ solution to a final concentration of $0.05 \text{ M}$, we use the dilution equation:

$M_1 V_1 = M_2 V_2$

$0.2 \times 300 = 0.05 \times V_2$

$V_2 = \dfrac{60}{0.05} = 1200 \text{ mL}$

The final volume of the solution is $1200 \text{ mL}$. The volume of water that must be added is:

$V_{\text{water}} = V_2 - V_1 = 1200 \text{ mL} - 300 \text{ mL} = 900 \text{ mL}$

Answer: $900$

questions.q:
A $20 \text{ mL}$ sample of an aqueous $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ solution is diluted to $200 \text{ mL}$. A $50 \text{ mL}$ portion of this diluted solution is mixed with $40 \text{ mL}$ of $0.5 \text{ M NaOH}$ solution. The resulting mixture requires $0.53 \text{ g}$ of $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ for complete neutralization. The molarity of the original $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ solution is ____ $\text{M}$. (Nearest integer)

[Given: Molar mass in $\text{g mol}^{-1}$: $\text{Na} = 23$, $\text{C} = 12$, $\text{O} = 16$]
questions.question:
A $20 \text{ mL}$ sample of an aqueous $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ solution is diluted to $200 \text{ mL}$. A $50 \text{ mL}$ portion of this diluted solution is mixed with $40 \text{ mL}$ of $0.5 \text{ M NaOH}$ solution. The resulting mixture requires $0.53 \text{ g}$ of $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ for complete neutralization. The molarity of the original $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ solution is ____ $\text{M}$. (Nearest integer)

[Given: Molar mass in $\text{g mol}^{-1}$: $\text{Na} = 23$, $\text{C} = 12$, $\text{O} = 16$]
questions.solution:
Let the molarity of the original $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ solution be $M$.

When $20 \text{ mL}$ of this solution is diluted to $200 \text{ mL}$, the molarity of the diluted solution becomes:
$M' = \dfrac{20 \times M}{200} = 0.1 M$

A $50 \text{ mL}$ portion of this diluted solution is taken. The number of millimoles of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ in this portion is:
$n_{\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4} = 50 \times 0.1 M = 5 M \text{ mmol}$

Since the $n$-factor of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is $2$, the milliequivalents (meq) of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is:
$\text{meq of acid} = 2 \times 5 M = 10 M$

This acid is neutralized by two bases: $\text{NaOH}$ and $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$.

Milliequivalents of $\text{NaOH}$ added:
$\text{meq of NaOH} = \text{Molarity} \times \text{Volume (mL)} \times n\text{-factor} = 0.5 \times 40 \times 1 = 20 \text{ meq}$

For $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$, the molar mass is:
$M_{\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3} = (2 \times 23) + 12 + (3 \times 16) = 106 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$

Moles of $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ added:
$n_{\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3} = \dfrac{0.53}{106} = 0.005 \text{ mol} = 5 \text{ mmol}$

Since the $n$-factor of $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ is $2$, its milliequivalents is:
$\text{meq of } \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 = 5 \times 2 = 10 \text{ meq}$

Total milliequivalents of base = $20 + 10 = 30 \text{ meq}$

For complete neutralization, the milliequivalents of acid must equal the total milliequivalents of base:
$10 M = 30$

$M = 3 \text{ M}$

Answer: $3$

A mixture of $\text{HCl}$ and $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is dissolved in water to make $50 \text{ mL}$ of a solution. The total concentration of $\text{H}^+$ ions in the solution is $0.12 \text{ M}$ (assuming complete dissociation of both acids). When the entire $50 \text{ mL}$ of this solution is treated with an excess of aqueous $\text{AgNO}_3$, $0.574 \text{ g}$ of a white precipitate is formed. The mass percentage of $\text{HCl}$ in the original mixture is ____. (Nearest integer)
Given: Molar masses (in $\text{g mol}^{-1}$): $\text{H} = 1$, $\text{O} = 16$, $\text{S} = 32$, $\text{Cl} = 35.5$, $\text{Ag} = 108$.
questions.question:
A mixture of $\text{HCl}$ and $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is dissolved in water to make $50 \text{ mL}$ of a solution. The total concentration of $\text{H}^+$ ions in the solution is $0.12 \text{ M}$ (assuming complete dissociation of both acids). When the entire $50 \text{ mL}$ of this solution is treated with an excess of aqueous $\text{AgNO}_3$, $0.574 \text{ g}$ of a white precipitate is formed. The mass percentage of $\text{HCl}$ in the original mixture is ____. (Nearest integer)
Given: Molar masses (in $\text{g mol}^{-1}$): $\text{H} = 1$, $\text{O} = 16$, $\text{S} = 32$, $\text{Cl} = 35.5$, $\text{Ag} = 108$.
questions.solution:
The white precipitate formed upon the addition of aqueous $\text{AgNO}_3$ is $\text{AgCl}$.

Molar mass of $\text{AgCl} = 108 + 35.5 = 143.5 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$.

Moles of $\text{AgCl}$ formed = $\dfrac{0.574}{143.5} = 0.004 \text{ mol}$.

Since $1 \text{ mol}$ of $\text{AgCl}$ is produced from $1 \text{ mol}$ of $\text{HCl}$, the moles of $\text{HCl}$ in the mixture is $n_{\text{HCl}} = 0.004 \text{ mol}$.

The total moles of $\text{H}^+$ ions in the $50 \text{ mL}$ ($0.05 \text{ L}$) solution is:
$n_{\text{H}^+} = \text{Molarity} \times \text{Volume} = 0.12 \text{ M} \times 0.05 \text{ L} = 0.006 \text{ mol}$.

Both acids dissociate completely. $\text{HCl}$ provides $1 \text{ H}^+$ per molecule, and $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ provides $2 \text{ H}^+$ per molecule. Thus:
$n_{\text{HCl}} + 2n_{\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4} = 0.006$

Substituting $n_{\text{HCl}} = 0.004 \text{ mol}$:
$0.004 + 2n_{\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4} = 0.006$

$2n_{\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4} = 0.002 \implies n_{\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4} = 0.001 \text{ mol}$.

Now, calculating the mass of each acid in the mixture:
Mass of $\text{HCl} = 0.004 \text{ mol} \times 36.5 \text{ g mol}^{-1} = 0.146 \text{ g}$
Mass of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 = 0.001 \text{ mol} \times 98 \text{ g mol}^{-1} = 0.098 \text{ g}$

Total mass of the mixture = $0.146 \text{ g} + 0.098 \text{ g} = 0.244 \text{ g}$.

The mass percentage of $\text{HCl}$ in the original mixture is:
$\text{Mass \%} = \dfrac{0.146}{0.244} \times 100 = \dfrac{146}{244} \times 100 \approx 59.836\%$

Rounding to the nearest integer, we get $60$.

Answer: $60$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A $0.30 \text{ g}$ sample of an anhydrous dibasic organic acid requires $40.0 \text{ mL}$ of $0.10 \text{ M}$ $\text{NaOH}$ solution for complete neutralization. A $0.51 \text{ g}$ sample of the hydrated form of the same acid requires $50.0 \text{ mL}$ of the same $\text{NaOH}$ solution for complete neutralization. The number of moles of water of crystallization present per mole of the hydrated acid is ____.
questions.question: A $0.30 \text{ g}$ sample of an anhydrous dibasic organic acid requires $40.0 \text{ mL}$ of $0.10 \text{ M}$ $\text{NaOH}$ solution for complete neutralization. A $0.51 \text{ g}$ sample of the hydrated form of the same acid requires $50.0 \text{ mL}$ of the same $\text{NaOH}$ solution for complete neutralization. The number of moles of water of crystallization present per mole of the hydrated acid is ____.
questions.solution:
Let the anhydrous dibasic acid be $H_2A$.

For the anhydrous acid, the neutralization reaction with $\text{NaOH}$ is:
$H_2A + 2\text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{Na}_2A + 2H_2O$

Moles of $\text{NaOH}$ used = $40.0 \times 10^{-3} \times 0.10 = 4.0 \times 10^{-3} \text{ mol}$

Moles of anhydrous acid = $\dfrac{1}{2} \times 4.0 \times 10^{-3} = 2.0 \times 10^{-3} \text{ mol}$

Molar mass of anhydrous acid ($M_a$) = $\dfrac{0.30}{2.0 \times 10^{-3}} = 150 \text{ g/mol}$

For the hydrated acid $H_2A \cdot nH_2O$, moles of $\text{NaOH}$ used = $50.0 \times 10^{-3} \times 0.10 = 5.0 \times 10^{-3} \text{ mol}$

Moles of hydrated acid = $\dfrac{1}{2} \times 5.0 \times 10^{-3} = 2.5 \times 10^{-3} \text{ mol}$

Molar mass of hydrated acid ($M_h$) = $\dfrac{0.51}{2.5 \times 10^{-3}} = 204 \text{ g/mol}$

The difference in molar mass is due to the water of crystallization:
$M_h - M_a = n \times 18$

$204 - 150 = 18n$

$18n = 54 \Rightarrow n = 3$

Answer: $3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A $100\text{ mL}$ sample of an aqueous solution of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ is completely oxidized by $100\text{ mL}$ of $0.1\text{ M KMnO}_4$ in acidic medium. An equal volume ($100\text{ mL}$) of the same $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ solution is completely oxidized by $V\text{ mL}$ of $0.1\text{ M KMnO}_4$ in faintly alkaline medium. The value of $V$ (rounded off to the nearest integer) is ________.
questions.question: A $100\text{ mL}$ sample of an aqueous solution of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ is completely oxidized by $100\text{ mL}$ of $0.1\text{ M KMnO}_4$ in acidic medium. An equal volume ($100\text{ mL}$) of the same $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ solution is completely oxidized by $V\text{ mL}$ of $0.1\text{ M KMnO}_4$ in faintly alkaline medium. The value of $V$ (rounded off to the nearest integer) is ________.
questions.solution:
In acidic medium, $\text{KMnO}_4$ is reduced to $\text{Mn}^{2+}$. The change in oxidation state of $\text{Mn}$ is from $+7$ to $+2$, so the n-factor is $5$.

Equivalents of $\text{KMnO}_4$ used in acidic medium = $n \times M \times V = 5 \times 0.1 \times 100 = 50$.

In faintly alkaline medium, $\text{KMnO}_4$ is reduced to $\text{MnO}_2$. The change in oxidation state of $\text{Mn}$ is from $+7$ to $+4$, so the n-factor is $3$.

Equivalents of $\text{KMnO}_4$ used in faintly alkaline medium = $n \times M \times V = 3 \times 0.1 \times V = 0.3V$.

The oxidation of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ yields $\text{O}_2$ in both acidic and faintly alkaline media, with an n-factor of $2$ in both cases. Since the same volume and concentration of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ is used, the number of equivalents of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ remains constant.

Equating the equivalents of $\text{KMnO}_4$ in both media:

$0.3V = 50$

$V = \dfrac{50}{0.3} = \dfrac{500}{3} = 166.66...$

Rounding off to the nearest integer gives $167$.

Answer: $167$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $1.50\text{ g}$ of a divalent metal carbonate $\text{MCO}_3$ was dissolved in $50\text{ mL}$ of $1.0\text{ M}$ $\text{HCl}$. The unreacted $\text{HCl}$ in the resulting solution requires $40\text{ mL}$ of $0.5\text{ M}$ $\text{NaOH}$ solution for complete neutralization. The molar mass of the metal carbonate is ____ $\text{g mol}^{-1}$.
questions.question: $1.50\text{ g}$ of a divalent metal carbonate $\text{MCO}_3$ was dissolved in $50\text{ mL}$ of $1.0\text{ M}$ $\text{HCl}$. The unreacted $\text{HCl}$ in the resulting solution requires $40\text{ mL}$ of $0.5\text{ M}$ $\text{NaOH}$ solution for complete neutralization. The molar mass of the metal carbonate is ____ $\text{g mol}^{-1}$.
questions.solution:
Total millimoles of $\text{HCl}$ initially present $= 50 \times 1.0 = 50\text{ mmol}$

Millimoles of $\text{NaOH}$ used to neutralize unreacted $\text{HCl} = 40 \times 0.5 = 20\text{ mmol}$

Since $\text{NaOH}$ reacts with $\text{HCl}$ in a $1:1$ molar ratio, millimoles of unreacted $\text{HCl} = 20\text{ mmol}$

Millimoles of $\text{HCl}$ reacted with $\text{MCO}_3 = 50 - 20 = 30\text{ mmol}$

The balanced chemical equation for the reaction is:

$\text{MCO}_3 + 2\text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{MCl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2$

From the stoichiometry, $1$ mole of $\text{MCO}_3$ reacts with $2$ moles of $\text{HCl}$.

Millimoles of $\text{MCO}_3$ reacted $= \dfrac{30}{2} = 15\text{ mmol} = 0.015\text{ mol}$

Molar mass of $\text{MCO}_3 = \dfrac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Moles}} = \dfrac{1.50}{0.015} = 100\text{ g mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $100$

Answer: $100$

questions.q:
A $0.921 \text{ g}$ sample of a mixture of $\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4$ and $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4$ was boiled with $100 \text{ mL}$ of $0.1 \text{ M}$ $\text{NaOH}$ until no more $\text{NH}_3$ gas was evolved. The excess $\text{NaOH}$ was neutralized by $30 \text{ mL}$ of $0.1 \text{ M}$ $\text{HCl}$. The mass of $\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4$ present in the mixture is ____ $\text{mg}$.

(Given molar masses in $\text{g mol}^{-1}$: $\text{H}=1$, $\text{N}=14$, $\text{O}=16$, $\text{Na}=23$, $\text{S}=32$)
questions.question:
A $0.921 \text{ g}$ sample of a mixture of $\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4$ and $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4$ was boiled with $100 \text{ mL}$ of $0.1 \text{ M}$ $\text{NaOH}$ until no more $\text{NH}_3$ gas was evolved. The excess $\text{NaOH}$ was neutralized by $30 \text{ mL}$ of $0.1 \text{ M}$ $\text{HCl}$. The mass of $\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4$ present in the mixture is ____ $\text{mg}$.

(Given molar masses in $\text{g mol}^{-1}$: $\text{H}=1$, $\text{N}=14$, $\text{O}=16$, $\text{Na}=23$, $\text{S}=32$)
questions.solution:
Initial millimoles of $\text{NaOH} = 100 \times 0.1 = 10 \text{ mmol}$

Millimoles of $\text{HCl}$ used to neutralize excess $\text{NaOH} = 30 \times 0.1 = 3 \text{ mmol}$

Millimoles of excess $\text{NaOH} = 3 \text{ mmol}$

Millimoles of $\text{NaOH}$ reacted with $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4 = 10 - 3 = 7 \text{ mmol}$

The reaction between ammonium sulfate and sodium hydroxide is:
$(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4 + 2\text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4 + 2\text{NH}_3 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$

From the stoichiometry, $1 \text{ mole}$ of $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4$ reacts with $2 \text{ moles}$ of $\text{NaOH}$.

Millimoles of $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4 = \dfrac{7}{2} = 3.5 \text{ mmol}$

Molar mass of $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4 = 2(14 + 4) + 32 + 4(16) = 132 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$

Mass of $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4 = 3.5 \text{ mmol} \times 132 \text{ mg mmol}^{-1} = 462 \text{ mg}$

Total mass of the mixture $= 0.921 \text{ g} = 921 \text{ mg}$

Mass of $\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4 = \text{Total mass} - \text{Mass of } (\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4$

Mass of $\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4 = 921 \text{ mg} - 462 \text{ mg} = 459 \text{ mg}$

Answer: $459$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
A $10 \text{ g}$ sample containing silver and silver sulphide ($\text{Ag}_2\text{S}$) is treated with excess hydrochloric acid. The reaction yields $11.2 \text{ mL}$ of $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ gas measured at $0^\circ\text{C}$ and $1 \text{ atm}$. The mass of silver sulphide present in the sample is _____ mg.
(Given: Molar mass of $\text{Ag} = 108 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$, $\text{S} = 32 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$. Molar volume of an ideal gas at $0^\circ\text{C}$ and $1 \text{ atm}$ is $22.4 \text{ L}$)
questions.question:
A $10 \text{ g}$ sample containing silver and silver sulphide ($\text{Ag}_2\text{S}$) is treated with excess hydrochloric acid. The reaction yields $11.2 \text{ mL}$ of $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ gas measured at $0^\circ\text{C}$ and $1 \text{ atm}$. The mass of silver sulphide present in the sample is _____ mg.
(Given: Molar mass of $\text{Ag} = 108 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$, $\text{S} = 32 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$. Molar volume of an ideal gas at $0^\circ\text{C}$ and $1 \text{ atm}$ is $22.4 \text{ L}$)
questions.solution:
The reaction of silver sulphide with hydrochloric acid is given by:

$\text{Ag}_2\text{S} + 2\text{HCl} \rightarrow 2\text{AgCl} + \text{H}_2\text{S}$

Silver ($\text{Ag}$) does not react with $\text{HCl}$ to produce $\text{H}_2\text{S}$.

Moles of $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ produced can be calculated using the given volume at STP ($0^{\circ}\text{C}$ and $1 \text{ atm}$):

$n_{\text{H}_2\text{S}} = \dfrac{11.2 \times 10^{-3} \text{ L}}{22.4 \text{ L mol}^{-1}} = 5 \times 10^{-4} \text{ mol}$

From the stoichiometry of the reaction, $1 \text{ mol}$ of $\text{Ag}_2\text{S}$ produces $1 \text{ mol}$ of $\text{H}_2\text{S}$.

$n_{\text{Ag}_2\text{S}} = n_{\text{H}_2\text{S}} = 5 \times 10^{-4} \text{ mol}$

The molar mass of $\text{Ag}_2\text{S}$ is:

$M_{\text{Ag}_2\text{S}} = 2 \times 108 + 32 = 248 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$

The mass of $\text{Ag}_2\text{S}$ present in the sample is:

$\text{Mass} = n_{\text{Ag}_2\text{S}} \times M_{\text{Ag}_2\text{S}} = 5 \times 10^{-4} \text{ mol} \times 248 \text{ g mol}^{-1} = 0.124 \text{ g}$

Converting the mass to milligrams:

$\text{Mass in mg} = 0.124 \times 1000 = 124 \text{ mg}$

Answer: $124$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
A $1.12 \text{ g}$ sample of iron wire containing $75\%$ iron is dissolved in dilute acid to completely convert the iron into $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ions. The resulting solution requires $25 \text{ mL}$ of an acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ solution for complete oxidation of $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ to $\text{Fe}^{3+}$. The molarity of the $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ solution is $x \times 10^{-2} \text{ M}$. The value of $x$ is ____.
(Given: Atomic mass of Fe = $56 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.question:
A $1.12 \text{ g}$ sample of iron wire containing $75\%$ iron is dissolved in dilute acid to completely convert the iron into $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ions. The resulting solution requires $25 \text{ mL}$ of an acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ solution for complete oxidation of $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ to $\text{Fe}^{3+}$. The molarity of the $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ solution is $x \times 10^{-2} \text{ M}$. The value of $x$ is ____.
(Given: Atomic mass of Fe = $56 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
Mass of pure iron in the sample = $1.12 \times \dfrac{75}{100} = 0.84 \text{ g}$

Moles of $\text{Fe}$ = $\dfrac{0.84}{56} = 0.015 \text{ mol}$

Since all iron is converted to $\text{Fe}^{2+}$, moles of $\text{Fe}^{2+} = 0.015 \text{ mol}$

The oxidation of $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ by $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ involves the following half-reactions:

$\text{Fe}^{2+} \rightarrow \text{Fe}^{3+} + e^{-}$ (n-factor = $1$)

$\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 14\text{H}^{+} + 6e^{-} \rightarrow 2\text{Cr}^{3+} + 7\text{H}_2\text{O}$ (n-factor = $6$)

By the principle of equivalence, equivalents of $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ = equivalents of $\text{Fe}^{2+}$

$M \times V(\text{in L}) \times n\text{-factor} = \text{Moles of Fe}^{2+} \times n\text{-factor}$

$M \times \dfrac{25}{1000} \times 6 = 0.015 \times 1$

$M \times 0.15 = 0.015$

$M = 0.1 \text{ M}$

$M = 10 \times 10^{-2} \text{ M}$

A $1.12 \text{ L}$ mixture of $\text{O}_2$ and $\text{O}_3$ at $273 \text{ K}$ and $1 \text{ atm}$ was passed through an excess of acidified $\text{KI}$ solution. The iodine liberated required $80 \text{ mL}$ of $0.5 \text{ M}$ sodium thiosulphate solution for complete titration. The mass percentage of ozone in the mixture is ________.
(Given: Molar volume of a gas at $273 \text{ K}$ and $1 \text{ atm}$ is $22.4 \text{ L}$)
questions.question:
A $1.12 \text{ L}$ mixture of $\text{O}_2$ and $\text{O}_3$ at $273 \text{ K}$ and $1 \text{ atm}$ was passed through an excess of acidified $\text{KI}$ solution. The iodine liberated required $80 \text{ mL}$ of $0.5 \text{ M}$ sodium thiosulphate solution for complete titration. The mass percentage of ozone in the mixture is ________.
(Given: Molar volume of a gas at $273 \text{ K}$ and $1 \text{ atm}$ is $22.4 \text{ L}$)
questions.solution:
Total moles of the gas mixture is given by:

$n_{\text{total}} = \dfrac{V}{V_m} = \dfrac{1.12}{22.4} = 0.05 \text{ mol}$

The reaction of ozone with acidified $\text{KI}$ is:

$\text{O}_3 + 2\text{I}^- + 2\text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{O}_2 + \text{I}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

The liberated iodine is titrated with sodium thiosulphate:

$\text{I}_2 + 2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-} \rightarrow 2\text{I}^- + \text{S}_4\text{O}_6^{2-}$

From the stoichiometry, $1 \text{ mole of } \text{O}_3 \equiv 1 \text{ mole of } \text{I}_2 \equiv 2 \text{ moles of } \text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-}$.

Moles of $\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-}$ used $= M \times V = 0.5 \times 80 \times 10^{-3} = 0.04 \text{ mol}$

Moles of $\text{O}_3$ in the mixture $= \dfrac{0.04}{2} = 0.02 \text{ mol}$

Moles of $\text{O}_2$ in the mixture $= 0.05 - 0.02 = 0.03 \text{ mol}$

Mass of $\text{O}_3 = 0.02 \times 48 = 0.96 \text{ g}$

Mass of $\text{O}_2 = 0.03 \times 32 = 0.96 \text{ g}$

Total mass of the mixture $= 0.96 + 0.96 = 1.92 \text{ g}$

Mass percentage of $\text{O}_3 = \dfrac{0.96}{1.92} \times 100 = 50\%$

Answer: $50$

A $50 \text{ mL}$ sample of chlorine water (density $= 1.0 \text{ g mL}^{-1}$) is treated with an excess of $\text{KI}$. The liberated iodine requires $40 \text{ mL}$ of $0.1 \text{ M Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3$ solution for complete titration. The percentage of $\text{Cl}_2$ (by mass) in the chlorine water is $x \times 10^{-3} \%$. The value of $x$ is ____.
(Given: Atomic mass of $\text{Cl} = 35.5 \text{ u}$)
questions.question:
A $50 \text{ mL}$ sample of chlorine water (density $= 1.0 \text{ g mL}^{-1}$) is treated with an excess of $\text{KI}$. The liberated iodine requires $40 \text{ mL}$ of $0.1 \text{ M Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3$ solution for complete titration. The percentage of $\text{Cl}_2$ (by mass) in the chlorine water is $x \times 10^{-3} \%$. The value of $x$ is ____.
(Given: Atomic mass of $\text{Cl} = 35.5 \text{ u}$)
questions.solution:
The reactions involved are:

$\text{Cl}_2 + 2\text{KI} \rightarrow 2\text{KCl} + \text{I}_2$

$\text{I}_2 + 2\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3 \rightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{S}_4\text{O}_6 + 2\text{NaI}$

From the stoichiometry, $1$ mole of $\text{Cl}_2$ produces $1$ mole of $\text{I}_2$, which reacts with $2$ moles of $\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3$.

Moles of $\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3$ used $= 40 \text{ mL} \times 0.1 \text{ M} = 4 \text{ mmol}$.

Moles of $\text{Cl}_2$ present $= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 4 \text{ mmol} = 2 \text{ mmol} = 2 \times 10^{-3} \text{ mol}$.

Mass of $\text{Cl}_2 = 2 \times 10^{-3} \text{ mol} \times 71 \text{ g mol}^{-1} = 0.142 \text{ g}$.

Mass of the chlorine water sample $= 50 \text{ mL} \times 1.0 \text{ g mL}^{-1} = 50 \text{ g}$.

Percentage of $\text{Cl}_2$ by mass $= \dfrac{0.142}{50} \times 100 = 0.284\%$.

Given that the percentage is $x \times 10^{-3}\%$, we have:

$x \times 10^{-3} = 0.284 \Rightarrow x = 284$.

Answer: $284$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
A household bleach solution contains hypochlorite ions ($\text{ClO}^{-}$), which are produced when chlorine gas is passed into an alkaline solution. To determine the concentration of hypochlorite, a $25.0 \text{ mL}$ sample of the bleach is treated with an excess of potassium iodide solution in an acidic medium. The iodine liberated during the reaction requires $17.4 \text{ mL}$ of a $0.02 \text{ M}$ sodium thiosulphate ($\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3$) solution for complete titration. The mass of chlorine used to prepare one litre of this bleach solution is ________ $\text{mg}$. (Nearest integer)
(Given : Molar mass of $\text{Cl} = 35.5 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.question:
A household bleach solution contains hypochlorite ions ($\text{ClO}^{-}$), which are produced when chlorine gas is passed into an alkaline solution. To determine the concentration of hypochlorite, a $25.0 \text{ mL}$ sample of the bleach is treated with an excess of potassium iodide solution in an acidic medium. The iodine liberated during the reaction requires $17.4 \text{ mL}$ of a $0.02 \text{ M}$ sodium thiosulphate ($\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3$) solution for complete titration. The mass of chlorine used to prepare one litre of this bleach solution is ________ $\text{mg}$. (Nearest integer)
(Given : Molar mass of $\text{Cl} = 35.5 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
The preparation of bleach by passing chlorine gas into an alkaline solution is given by the reaction:
$\text{Cl}_2 + 2\text{OH}^{-} \rightarrow \text{ClO}^{-} + \text{Cl}^{-} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$
From this, $1$ mole of $\text{Cl}_2$ produces $1$ mole of hypochlorite ($\text{ClO}^{-}$).

When the bleach is treated with excess potassium iodide in an acidic medium, $\text{ClO}^{-}$ oxidizes $\text{I}^{-}$ to $\text{I}_2$:
$\text{ClO}^{-} + 2\text{I}^{-} + 2\text{H}^{+} \rightarrow \text{Cl}^{-} + \text{I}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$
Here, $1$ mole of $\text{ClO}^{-}$ liberates $1$ mole of $\text{I}_2$.

The liberated iodine is titrated with sodium thiosulphate:
$\text{I}_2 + 2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-} \rightarrow 2\text{I}^{-} + \text{S}_4\text{O}_6^{2-}$
Here, $1$ mole of $\text{I}_2$ reacts with $2$ moles of $\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-}$.

Moles of $\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-}$ used in the titration:
$n(\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-}) = 17.4 \text{ mL} \times 0.02 \text{ M} = 0.348 \text{ mmol}$

Moles of $\text{I}_2$ produced:
$n(\text{I}_2) = \dfrac{0.348}{2} = 0.174 \text{ mmol}$

Moles of $\text{ClO}^{-}$ in the $25.0 \text{ mL}$ sample:
$n(\text{ClO}^{-}) = 0.174 \text{ mmol}$

Moles of $\text{Cl}_2$ used to produce this amount of $\text{ClO}^{-}$ in $25.0 \text{ mL}$:
$n(\text{Cl}_2) = 0.174 \text{ mmol}$

To find the moles of $\text{Cl}_2$ used for one litre ($1000 \text{ mL}$) of the bleach solution:
$n(\text{Cl}_2)_{1\text{L}} = 0.174 \text{ mmol} \times \dfrac{1000 \text{ mL}}{25.0 \text{ mL}} = 0.174 \times 40 = 6.96 \text{ mmol}$

Mass of chlorine ($\text{Cl}_2$) used:
$\text{Mass} = 6.96 \text{ mmol} \times 71 \text{ g mol}^{-1} = 494.16 \text{ mg}$

Rounding to the nearest integer, we get $494 \text{ mg}$.

Answer: $494$

$\text{AsO}_4^{3-} + 2\text{H}^+ + 2\text{I}^- \rightarrow \text{AsO}_3^{3-} + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{I}_2$
The volume of the thiosulphate solution consumed is ____ $\text{mL}$.
(Given: Molar mass of $\text{As} = 75 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$, $\text{Na} = 23 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$, $\text{O} = 16 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.question:

The iodine evolved is absorbed in $\text{KI}$ solution and titrated against a $0.25 \text{ M}$ sodium thiosulphate ($\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3$) solution. Assuming the reaction to be:
$\text{AsO}_4^{3-} + 2\text{H}^+ + 2\text{I}^- \rightarrow \text{AsO}_3^{3-} + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{I}_2$
The volume of the thiosulphate solution consumed is ____ $\text{mL}$.
(Given: Molar mass of $\text{As} = 75 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$, $\text{Na} = 23 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$, $\text{O} = 16 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
The molar mass of $\text{Na}_3\text{AsO}_4$ is calculated as:
$3 \times 23 + 75 + 4 \times 16 = 69 + 75 + 64 = 208 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$

Number of moles of $\text{Na}_3\text{AsO}_4$ is:
$n = \dfrac{1.04}{208} = 0.005 \text{ mol}$

From the given balanced chemical equation:
$\text{AsO}_4^{3-} + 2\text{H}^+ + 2\text{I}^- \rightarrow \text{AsO}_3^{3-} + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{I}_2$
We can see that $1 \text{ mol}$ of $\text{AsO}_4^{3-}$ produces $1 \text{ mol}$ of $\text{I}_2$.
Therefore, moles of $\text{I}_2$ produced $= 0.005 \text{ mol}$.

The liberated iodine is titrated against sodium thiosulphate according to the reaction:
$\text{I}_2 + 2\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3 \rightarrow 2\text{NaI} + \text{Na}_2\text{S}_4\text{O}_6$

From the stoichiometry, $1 \text{ mol}$ of $\text{I}_2$ reacts with $2 \text{ mol}$ of $\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3$.
Moles of $\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3$ required $= 2 \times 0.005 = 0.01 \text{ mol}$.

Given the molarity of $\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3$ solution is $0.25 \text{ M}$, the volume $V$ in liters is:
$V = \dfrac{\text{Moles}}{\text{Molarity}} = \dfrac{0.01}{0.25} = 0.04 \text{ L}$

Converting to milliliters:
$V = 0.04 \times 1000 = 40 \text{ mL}$

Answer: $40$

$V = \dfrac{0.02}{0.5} = 0.04 \text{ L}$

$V = 0.04 \times 1000 = 40 \text{ mL}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In an acidic medium, $V_1 \text{ mL}$ of a potassium permanganate ($\text{KMnO}_4$) solution of molarity $M_1$ reacts completely with $V_2 \text{ mL}$ of an aqueous ferrous sulphate ($\text{FeSO}_4$) solution of molarity $M_2$. Which of the following relationships is correct?
questions.question: In an acidic medium, $V_1 \text{ mL}$ of a potassium permanganate ($\text{KMnO}_4$) solution of molarity $M_1$ reacts completely with $V_2 \text{ mL}$ of an aqueous ferrous sulphate ($\text{FeSO}_4$) solution of molarity $M_2$. Which of the following relationships is correct?
questions.solution:
In an acidic medium, the reduction half-reaction for potassium permanganate is:

$\text{MnO}_4^- + 8\text{H}^+ + 5\text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{Mn}^{2+} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$

The n-factor for $\text{KMnO}_4$ is $5$.

The oxidation half-reaction for ferrous sulphate is:

$\text{Fe}^{2+} \rightarrow \text{Fe}^{3+} + \text{e}^-$

The n-factor for $\text{FeSO}_4$ is $1$.

According to the law of equivalence, for a complete reaction, the number of equivalents of the oxidizing agent must equal the number of equivalents of the reducing agent.

$\text{Equivalents of } \text{KMnO}_4 = \text{Equivalents of } \text{FeSO}_4$

$n_1 \times M_1 \times V_1 = n_2 \times M_2 \times V_2$

$5 \times M_1 \times V_1 = 1 \times M_2 \times V_2$

$5V_1M_1 = V_2M_2$

Answer: $5V_1M_1 = V_2M_2$
questions.explanation:
In an acidic medium, the reduction half-reaction for potassium permanganate is:

$\text{MnO}_4^- + 8\text{H}^+ + 5\text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{Mn}^{2+} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$

The n-factor for $\text{KMnO}_4$ is $5$.

The oxidation half-reaction for ferrous sulphate is:

$\text{Fe}^{2+} \rightarrow \text{Fe}^{3+} + \text{e}^-$

The n-factor for $\text{FeSO}_4$ is $1$.

According to the law of equivalence, for a complete reaction, the number of equivalents of the oxidizing agent must equal the number of equivalents of the reducing agent.

$\text{Equivalents of } \text{KMnO}_4 = \text{Equivalents of } \text{FeSO}_4$

$n_1 \times M_1 \times V_1 = n_2 \times M_2 \times V_2$

$5 \times M_1 \times V_1 = 1 \times M_2 \times V_2$

$5V_1M_1 = V_2M_2$

Answer: $5V_1M_1 = V_2M_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For complete oxidation, $x \text{ g}$ of $\text{NaHC}_2\text{O}_4$ requires $40 \text{ mL}$ of $0.05 \text{ M KMnO}_4$ in an acidic medium. In a separate experiment, $y \text{ g}$ of $\text{NaHC}_2\text{O}_4$ requires $25 \text{ mL}$ of $0.20 \text{ M Ca(OH)}_2$ for complete neutralization. The value of $\dfrac{y}{x}$ is ____.
questions.question: For complete oxidation, $x \text{ g}$ of $\text{NaHC}_2\text{O}_4$ requires $40 \text{ mL}$ of $0.05 \text{ M KMnO}_4$ in an acidic medium. In a separate experiment, $y \text{ g}$ of $\text{NaHC}_2\text{O}_4$ requires $25 \text{ mL}$ of $0.20 \text{ M Ca(OH)}_2$ for complete neutralization. The value of $\dfrac{y}{x}$ is ____.
questions.solution:
For the oxidation of $\text{NaHC}_2\text{O}_4$ by $\text{KMnO}_4$ in an acidic medium, the active reducing part is the oxalate ion ($\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$), which oxidizes to $\text{CO}_2$.
The n-factor of $\text{NaHC}_2\text{O}_4$ in this reaction is $2$.
The n-factor of $\text{KMnO}_4$ in an acidic medium is $5$.

Equating the equivalents of $\text{NaHC}_2\text{O}_4$ and $\text{KMnO}_4$:
$\dfrac{x}{M} \times 2 = \dfrac{40 \times 0.05 \times 5}{1000}$

$\dfrac{2x}{M} = 0.01 \Rightarrow \dfrac{x}{M} = 0.005$

For the neutralization of $\text{NaHC}_2\text{O}_4$ by $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$, the active acidic part is the hydrogen oxalate ion ($\text{HC}_2\text{O}_4^{-}$), which has one replaceable proton.
The n-factor of $\text{NaHC}_2\text{O}_4$ in this reaction is $1$.
The n-factor of $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$ is $2$.

Equating the equivalents of $\text{NaHC}_2\text{O}_4$ and $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$:
$\dfrac{y}{M} \times 1 = \dfrac{25 \times 0.20 \times 2}{1000}$

$\dfrac{y}{M} = 0.01$

Taking the ratio of the two equations:
$\dfrac{y/M}{x/M} = \dfrac{0.01}{0.005}$

$\dfrac{y}{x} = 2$

Answer: $2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A solution containing a mixture of $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ and $\text{NaHCO}_3$ is titrated against a standard $\text{HCl}$ solution. Using phenolphthalein as an indicator, $V_1\text{ mL}$ of the acid is required to reach the end point. Subsequently, methyl orange is added to the same solution and the titration is continued. An additional $V_2\text{ mL}$ of the same $\text{HCl}$ solution is required to reach the second end point. The volume of $\text{HCl}$ required for the complete neutralization of the $\text{NaHCO}_3$ originally present in the mixture is:
questions.question: A solution containing a mixture of $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ and $\text{NaHCO}_3$ is titrated against a standard $\text{HCl}$ solution. Using phenolphthalein as an indicator, $V_1\text{ mL}$ of the acid is required to reach the end point. Subsequently, methyl orange is added to the same solution and the titration is continued. An additional $V_2\text{ mL}$ of the same $\text{HCl}$ solution is required to reach the second end point. The volume of $\text{HCl}$ required for the complete neutralization of the $\text{NaHCO}_3$ originally present in the mixture is:
questions.solution:
In the presence of phenolphthalein indicator, only half of the neutralization of $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ takes place. The reaction is:

$\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 + \text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{NaHCO}_3 + \text{NaCl}$

The volume of $\text{HCl}$ required for this step is $V_1$. This means the volume of $\text{HCl}$ equivalent to half of the $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ is $V_1$.

When methyl orange is added and the titration is continued, the $\text{NaHCO}_3$ present in the solution is neutralized. This $\text{NaHCO}_3$ consists of two parts:
1. The $\text{NaHCO}_3$ formed from the initial $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$, which will require an equal volume $V_1$ of $\text{HCl}$ for complete neutralization.
2. The $\text{NaHCO}_3$ originally present in the mixture.

The reaction for this step is:

$\text{NaHCO}_3 + \text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{NaCl} + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2$

The total volume of $\text{HCl}$ required for this second step is given as $V_2$.

Therefore, we can write:
$V_2 = (\text{Volume of HCl for } \text{NaHCO}_3 \text{ formed from } \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3) + (\text{Volume of HCl for original } \text{NaHCO}_3)$

$V_2 = V_1 + (\text{Volume of HCl for original } \text{NaHCO}_3)$

$\text{Volume of HCl for original } \text{NaHCO}_3 = V_2 - V_1$

Answer: $(V_2 - V_1)\text{ mL}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
A $20 \text{ mL}$ sample of $0.15 \text{ M}$ $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ solution is titrated with $0.12 \text{ M}$ $\text{NaOH}$ solution. When bromocresol green is used as the indicator, $25 \text{ mL}$ of the base is required to reach the end point. When the same $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ sample is titrated using phenolphthalein as the indicator, $50 \text{ mL}$ of the base is required. The net reaction occurring in the second titration (with phenolphthalein) is represented as:
$\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 + n\text{OH}^- \rightarrow [\text{H}_{3-n}\text{PO}_4]^{n-} + n\text{H}_2\text{O}$
The value of $n$ is ____.
questions.question:
A $20 \text{ mL}$ sample of $0.15 \text{ M}$ $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ solution is titrated with $0.12 \text{ M}$ $\text{NaOH}$ solution. When bromocresol green is used as the indicator, $25 \text{ mL}$ of the base is required to reach the end point. When the same $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ sample is titrated using phenolphthalein as the indicator, $50 \text{ mL}$ of the base is required. The net reaction occurring in the second titration (with phenolphthalein) is represented as:
$\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 + n\text{OH}^- \rightarrow [\text{H}_{3-n}\text{PO}_4]^{n-} + n\text{H}_2\text{O}$
The value of $n$ is ____.
questions.solution:
Millimoles of $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ in the sample $= 20 \text{ mL} \times 0.15 \text{ M} = 3.0 \text{ mmol}$

In the second titration using phenolphthalein as the indicator, the volume of $\text{NaOH}$ required is $50 \text{ mL}$.

Millimoles of $\text{NaOH}$ used $= 50 \text{ mL} \times 0.12 \text{ M} = 6.0 \text{ mmol}$

The net reaction is given by:
$\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 + n\text{OH}^- \rightarrow [\text{H}_{3-n}\text{PO}_4]^{n-} + n\text{H}_2\text{O}$

From the stoichiometry of the reaction, $n$ moles of $\text{OH}^-$ react with $1$ mole of $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$.

$n = \dfrac{\text{Millimoles of NaOH}}{\text{Millimoles of H}_3\text{PO}_4} = \dfrac{6.0}{3.0} = 2$

Answer: $2$
